finding_1_create_admin_is_open.what_it_does_in_source: runs with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY; auth.admin.createUser({email,password,email_confirm:true}), and when the email already exists it looks the user up with listUsers() and calls auth.admin.updateUserById(id,{password})
measured: POST with apikey+Authorization anon headers -> 400 {"error":"Email and password required"}
POST with NO apikey and NO Authorization header at all -> 400 {"error":"Email and password required"}
finding_1_create_admin_is_open.reading: the 400 is the handler's own validation message, so the request reached the function body with no credentials of any kind. The route is deployed and ungated. Anyone who knows the URL can set the password of any account in this project by email.
finding_1_create_admin_is_open.not_done_on_purpose: no account was created and no password was overwritten. The probe deliberately omitted the password field so the handler would return before touching auth.admin. Reachability is proven by the handler answering, not by exercising the takeover.
finding_1_create_admin_is_open.why_verify_jwt_alone_would_not_fix_it: the anon key is a valid JWT and ships in the browser bundle, so a JWT gate is satisfied by anything that can load the page
finding_1_create_admin_is_open.fix_in_this_commit: the function now requires ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_SECRET (env-only, never sent to a browser) in the x-admin-bootstrap-secret header, answers 503 when the secret is not configured and 404 when it does not match. NOT DEPLOYED — deploying to this Supabase project needs credentials this environment does not have (NEEDS_USER).

finding_2_create_admin_never_created_an_.detail: migration 20260712192546 gates every admin path on has_role(auth.uid(),'admin'), which reads public.user_roles; only service_role can write to user_roles. create-admin created an auth user and stopped there, so the account it produced could never pass /mthbram/admin-login.
measured: sign-in l023131500@gmail.com / More30Admin2026 -> 400 (no such account with that password)
sign-in test@more30.com / More30Test2026 -> 200, user 6b0907f4-acae-42d6-8d79-3b07c49f9976, rpc has_role(uid,'admin') -> false
GET /rest/v1/user_roles as that signed-in user -> [] (policy 'Users can view own roles' — this user holds no role)
finding_2_create_admin_never_created_an_.reading: no account known to this project's own documentation can enter the admin console. Nothing here proves the role table is globally empty — only an admin could read that — but every credential §1ב names was tried and none passes.
finding_2_create_admin_never_created_an_.fix_in_this_commit: create-admin now upserts {user_id, role:'admin'} into user_roles after creating or resetting the account, so the function finally does what its name says. Same deploy blocker as finding 1.
